facts.raw_span: multiple asymptomatic, skin-colored nodules over his neck, trunk, and upper limbs
no fever
no lymphadenopathy
discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules measuring 0.5–2 cm in diameter
no overlying erythema, warmth, or tenderness
a single firm, non-tender nodule was palpated on the lateral tongue
vital signs were normal
complete blood count and metabolic profile, were within normal limits
Serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C viruses were nonreactive
no weight loss
no neurologic symptoms
the lesions had slowly increased in size and number

concepts.why: The patient presents with multiple asymptomatic, skin-colored nodules, which are characteristic of neurofibromas, and the lesions have slowly increased in size and number.
The patient has discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules, which are consistent with lipomas, and the lack of overlying erythema, warmth, or tenderness supports this diagnosis.
The patient presents with skin-colored nodules, which could be dermatofibromas, and the normal vital signs and lack of systemic complaints support this diagnosis.
The patient has firm, non-tender nodules, which are consistent with fibromas, and the normal laboratory investigations support this diagnosis.
